frameworkCheck.title: AP U.S. History Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2026)
frameworkCheck.how: The 105 numbered CED topics (1.1–9.7) were read from the current PDF on AP Central, and each is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions teach it. Each period's first topic (contextualizing the period) and its final reasoning topic (comparison, causation, or continuity and change) are covered by the topic whose questions practice that skill. The CED's six historical thinking skills (Developments and Processes; Sourcing and Situation; Claims and Evidence in Sources; Contextualization; Making Connections; Argumentation) and three reasoning processes (Comparison; Causation; Continuity and Change) were also checked; StudySprint's multiple-choice questions practice the first five skills (College Board notes that no multiple-choice questions assess Argumentation).
frameworkCheck.weightsSource: the AP Students course page (“On The Exam”) and the CED's exam section, both checked 2026-11-08
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page and the CED clarifications (beginning with the May 2027 exam): Section IA, 55 multiple-choice questions in 55 minutes (40% of the score), in sets of usually 3–4 questions about the same source or sources; Section IB, 3 required short-answer questions in 40 minutes (20%), each with source material; Section II, a document-based question (25%, 7 documents, 60 minutes recommended including a 15-minute reading period) and one required long essay (15%, 40 minutes). StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only, in source-based sets; written-response practice uses College Board's released questions.
differences: Several topic titles differ slightly between the CED's Course at a Glance and its topic pages (for example 3.6 “The Influence of Revolutionary Ideals” and “Social Consequences of Revolutionary Ideals”, 8.5 “Culture after 1945” and “Culture from 1945 to 1960”, and 9.2 “Reagan and Conservatism” and “Reagan and Conservativism”). StudySprint records the topic-page titles as printed.

The CED clarifications for Fall 2026 change the short-answer and long-essay sections (all three short-answer questions are required and include sources; one long essay is required); the AP Students assessment page already describes the new format.

generalResources.title: OpenStax U.S. History (whole book)
generalResources.note: General: a free college U.S. history textbook from the pre-Columbian era to the present. Its chapters don't line up one-to-one with the AP periods.
generalResources.licenseOrRights: Linked only. OpenStax lists U.S. History under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Its own text was not copied or adapted here; public-domain primary sources quoted in StudySprint's questions follow its excerpts and are credited.
